GAP-01; SOURCE_GAP; MATERIAL; Epiq's own financial statements, results, pro forma data and purchase price allocation are in no supplied document. Epiq closed on 2026-09-30, after the 2026-09-28 balance sheet, and the filing says the information needed for the initial accounting has not been received; Financial foundation and Fundamental credit report pre-Epiq figures; any pro forma leverage is an estimate built from stated amounts. Also limits Earnings changes, Downside, Liquidity, Forward credit model; The filing says the preliminary accounting will be in the fourth quarter of 2026 report; or supply Epiq's financial statements; Open; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24

GAP-02; SOURCE_GAP; MINOR; No executed credit agreement or indenture is supplied (run settings declare none), and no covenant ratio value is printed; the filings state compliance and the revolver tests of minimum interest coverage 2.50x and maximum leverage 4.50x; Covenant definitions, baskets and headroom cannot be established; Legal & covenants, Recovery & fulcrum and Security selection are conditional; Supply the executed documents listed in the exhibit index as filed with current reports on 2026-08-17, 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-30, and compliance certificates; Open; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 46

GAP-03; SOURCE_GAP; MINOR; No earnings release, presentation, non-GAAP reconciliation or management bridge; no adjusted EBITDA appears in any of the five filings, which mention EBITDA only in a glossary and as a pay-plan metric; EBITDA must be built from operating income plus depreciation and amortization in the cash flow statements, without management add-backs; Earnings quality is conditional; Supply earnings releases and reconciliations; Open; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6

GAP-04; SOURCE_GAP; MINOR; No agency ratings, market quotes, peer data, portfolio file or proxy statement: run settings leave ratings, quotes and peers empty, no filing names a rating agency, and the annual report defers director, pay and ownership disclosure to a proxy statement; Ratings & triggers, Market-implied risk, Peer benchmark and Security selection are conditional; board independence and ownership are not established; Supply the items if those analyses are wanted; Open; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, pages 77–78

GAP-05; STALE_EVIDENCE; MINOR; The latest document was signed on 2026-10-28 and the as-of date is 2026-11-18; no document after 2026-10-28 is supplied; Events in the 21 days between are not captured, including any update on the pending Ophir Optics purchase; Add later filings if the as-of date is to be kept; Open; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 47

GAP-06; COVERAGE_GAP; MINOR; Segment basis changed twice: the FY2024 annual report reports two segments (PCB and RF&S Components), the FY2025 annual report reports three (A&D, Commercial and RF&S Components) with FY2024 and FY2023 recast, and the 2026 reports report two (A&D and Commercial) with recast comparatives for 2025 interim periods only; No annual segment series is on the 2026 basis, so annual segment history does not compare with 2026 segment figures; Use consolidated figures for trend; treat segment trend as a limitation; Open; 10-K_2024-12-30_ttmi-20241230.htm.jsonl, page 139; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, pages 102–103; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 11

GAP-07; PREPARATION_GAP; MINOR; The text extractions flatten tables to one cell per line, split the closing bracket of negative figures from the figure, and divide filings into chunks of about 3,000 characters that do not match printed pages, so a table header can sit on the chunk before its figures; Risk of misreading a flattened table; mitigated for the statements by the foot checks above; Read tables with the header chunk; cite chunk numbers as pages; Open; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 20

CONFLICT-01; Definition conflict; MINOR; The 2026 reports say the Amended Term Loan Facility requires quarterly principal repayments equal to 1% of the 400,000 initial principal, which reads as 4,000 a quarter; the year-end 2025 report says quarterly repayments in an aggregate annual amount equal to 1% of the principal, and the balance sheet shows 4,000 as the current portion of the term loan; Scheduled amortization of the term loan is ambiguous in the 2026 wording; the annual reading fits the balance sheet; Financial foundation should use the annual reading shown by the current portion and the maturity table, and flag the wording; Open; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 106; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15

CONFLICT-02; Definition conflict; MINOR; The Q3 2026 risk factor says the credit agreements contain financial covenants requiring a consolidated fixed-charge coverage ratio under certain events, while the debt note describes maintenance tests of interest coverage and leverage on the revolver only; the earlier asset-based facilities that used a fixed-charge test ended on 2026-06-01; The covenant set to be tested is not stated consistently; Take the debt note as the covenant statement and flag the risk factor wording; Open; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 108

rows.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view — paragraph 1

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- Epiq's financial statements, results, balance sheet and purchase price allocation are not in any supplied document, so pro forma leverage cannot include Epiq's earnings, cash or debt; it restricts the post-closing leverage, cover and liquidity figures, severity High, and the action is the fourth quarter 2026 report or Epiq's own statements. - The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA is built from operating income plus depreciation and amortization for every period; it restricts comparison with lender-defined leverage and with covenant tests, severity Medium, and the action is an earnings release with a reconciliation. - Covenant ratio values and definitions for the revolver tests are not printed, so covenant headroom is not calculable for any period; severity Medium, and the action is the executed credit agreement and compliance certificates. - The undrawn committed facilities at the end of FY2023 are not in the supplied annual reports, so the FY2023 liquidity row has cash only; severity Low, and the action is the FY2023 annual report. - Several income statement and cash flow cells are dashes in the source (impairment of goodwill, loss on extinguishment of debt, gain on sale of subsidiary, derivative losses, proceeds of capital-related government incentives and others) and are written as not supplied, not zero; severity Low, and the action is none beyond confirming the dashes mean nil. - Some lines exist in only some reports (for example derivative losses appear only in the 2026 interim statements and purchases of equipment are gross in annual reports and net in interim reports), so those cells are not supplied for the other columns; severity Medium for capital spending, which makes last-twelve-months capital spending and free cash flow not calculable, and the action is a consistent capital spending series. - The 2026 wording on term loan repayments is ambiguous between a quarterly and an annual 1% of the original principal; it restricts the scheduled amortization shown for the term loan; severity Medium, and the action is the credit agreement. - Segment reporting changed in 2025 and again in 2026 and no annual series is on the 2026 basis, so segment trend across annual and interim periods is not comparable; severity Medium, and the action is a recast annual segment table. - Acquisition accounting for Swiss Technology Group AG is provisional and the filing presents no pro forma information, so goodwill, intangibles and the post-acquisition earnings contribution may change; severity Low, and the action is the fourth quarter 2026 report. - No quarterly statement for the fourth quarter of 2025 is supplied, so that quarter is derived as the full year less nine months and labelled calculated; severity Low, and the action is none. - Period start dates are not printed and are set to the day after the previous period end; severity Low, and the action is none. - The share of cash held by foreign subsidiaries, USD 241.1 million at 2026-09-28, may be subject to repatriation tax if remitted, although the issuer states no material unaccrued tax; severity Low, and the action is none. - Capital spending is not split between maintenance and growth in any filing, so those lines are not supplied; severity Medium, and the action is management disclosure of the split. - The pending Ophir Optics acquisition is not completed, so no net debt effect or pro forma figure is stated for it and its cells are not supplied; severity Low, and the action is the report after closing. - The share repurchase is dated as a two-day window and not by purchase, so its date cell is not supplied; severity Low, and the action is none. - No balance sheet at the end of the third quarter of 2025 is supplied, so the period-end working capital measures have no nine-month 2025 value; severity Low, and the action is none.

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is earnings momentum and liquidity. Third-quarter segment operating margin was 18.5% in aerospace and defense and 21.1% in Commercial, against 16.3% and 14.7% a year earlier. Epiq is described as adding critical technologies for defense customers, which, if its earnings are defense-linked and stable, would rebalance the mix toward aerospace and defense. Against that, the 75.3% fixed-rate share of debt predates the floating-rate term loans, and the cash balance appears to include the proceeds of the 2034 notes raised four days before quarter end, which were used after quarter end. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Earnings, not debt reduction, repaired the credit. Carrying debt was USD 917.8 million at FY2023 and USD 916.2 million at FY2025, yet total leverage fell from 4.52x to 2.22x as EBITDA doubled. It was 2.81x on a last-twelve-months basis at 2026-09-28, after the 2026 borrowings for the Swiss purchase and for Epiq. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G1; calculation G2

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against caution is that the earnings base is large and still rising: EBITDA margin reached 15.3% on a last-twelve-months basis, reported net leverage was only 1.31x before Epiq, management states covenant compliance, and long-term defense contracts carried USD 463.5 million of remaining obligations at 2026-09-28. If Epiq earns material EBITDA, the 3.20x overstates leverage, and the Incremental Facilities equal the Epiq price, so the revolver headroom was largely preserved. Epiq is described as adding technology for defense customers, which could rebalance a mix that is now led by data center sales. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The main strengths are these. First, earnings have more than doubled since FY2023 and drove total leverage from 4.52x to 2.22x at FY2025, which gives the debt a much larger earnings base and lowers refinancing risk. Second, liquidity of USD 1,610.2 million at 2026-09-28 and a maturity ladder with only USD 181.0 million due before 2029 give time to digest the acquisitions. Third, the defense franchise is anchored in long-term contracts with USD 463.5 million of remaining performance obligations and a US Navy radar position, which supports a steadier base beside the data center cycle. Fourth, margin gains in both segments show operating leverage working in the issuer's favour while volumes are high. Fifth, there is no sponsor and no dividend, so no external owner draws cash out. facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: The main weaknesses are these. First, the Epiq purchase and the pending Ophir Optics purchase raise net leverage to 3.20x pro forma while the target's earnings are unseen, which makes the next two quarters decisive for creditors. facts.label: Company description
facts.text: TTM Technologies makes printed circuit boards, RF and microwave components and assemblies, and engineered mission systems, and sells to equipment makers, contract manufacturers, distributors and governments. About 59% of nine-month net sales came from operations outside the United States, revenue is mostly recognized over time as customer-specific products are built, and the business is not seasonal. The credit link is that long-term defense contracts and a diversified customer list support cash-flow visibility, while the AI-driven commercial boom, high fixed costs and acquisition debt make debt service more cyclical than the defense history alone would suggest. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue rests on two engines: defense electronics sold through government budgets and long-term contracts, and commercial circuit boards for AI data centers, automotive and medical customers. Data center and networking was 39% of nine-month net sales against 30%, aerospace and defense 37% against 45%, and long-term defense contracts carried USD 463.5 million of remaining obligations with about 55% to be recognized within 12 months. Pricing power is only partly evidenced: gross margin rose 2.0 percentage points to 22.4% on volume and mix, quick-turn work earns premium pricing, but no contract pass-through of raw material costs is described. Revenue is therefore predictable in defense, cyclical and concentrated in data center and networking, and moderately recurring overall; the implication is that cash flow durability is adequate rather than strong. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation G12

facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: Management states that operating costs are relatively fixed and that small revenue shortfalls reduce operating margin, so operating leverage works both ways: gross margin rose to 22.4% and operating margin to 11.3% on higher volume, and the same fixed base would amplify a slowdown. Unallocated corporate costs are also growing, with stock-based compensation of USD 61.7 million against USD 29.6 million and other corporate costs of USD 103.5 million against USD 66.4 million in nine months, which reduces the margin that segment profit converts into group profit. Raw materials such as copper and gold are exposed to price swings and some components have sole sources. Margins can be defended against moderate volume pressure, but not against a sharp fall in data center orders. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Rivalry is intense: printed circuit boards are fragmented with larger, lower-cost Chinese and Taiwanese competitors, while defense systems compete with BAE Systems, Curtiss-Wright, Leonardo DRS, Mercury Systems and Sanmina; the implication is price pressure in commercial boards and a premium for qualified defense work. New entrants face facility security clearances and customer qualification in defense, while the annual report notes that new competitors may enter commercial boards, which limits pricing power there. Buyer power is high because a few customers and contract manufacturers account for a large share of sales and receivables. Supplier power is moderate: laminates and chemicals are broadly available, but some components for assemblies have limited or sole sources. Substitution risk is not discussed in the documents read. facts.label: Macro and policy factors
facts.text: Policy and currency factors are material to this credit. Both the US and Chinese governments have put circuit boards under tariffs, about 59% of nine-month sales come from non-US operations, and costs and cash are exposed to the Chinese yuan, Malaysian ringgit and Swiss franc, with a net investment hedge on the Swiss purchase. Defense sales depend on US budget appropriations and contract terminations, and export rules shape competition. The credit effect is margin and cash volatility that is partly outside management's control. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are AI data center capacity demand, defense budgets and program bookings, and new capacity at Eau Claire, Penang and Syracuse, which together support growth and margin. The headwinds are integration of STG, Epiq and Ophir Optics, capital spending that exceeds operating cash flow, higher interest on floating-rate loans, tariffs and currency swings. Over three to five years the main questions are whether AI demand proves durable rather than cyclical, whether Epiq earnings cover its price, and whether the 2029 notes and 2030 term loan balance are refinanced at acceptable cost; refinancing confidence rests on earnings, which is why a data center slowdown is the key risk to it. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a pause in AI data center orders or the loss of volume at one of the largest customers; one customer was about 20% of third-quarter sales and the five largest were 44% of nine-month sales. The first operational break is lower volume in the Commercial segment, whose fixed cost base would cut margin quickly, and that segment supplied more profit than the whole group. Financially, EBITDA falls while the pro forma net debt of USD 1,867.5 million stays, so net leverage rises above 3.20x, free cash flow turns negative because committed capital spending continues, and the cash cushion funds the gap. Management levers are slowing growth capital spending, suspending repurchases and not closing Ophir Optics; whether they suffice depends on the maintenance share of spending, which is not stated, and on covenant definitions, which are not supplied. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in a moderate downturn because liquidity was large and no large maturity falls before 2029, but leverage-based tests and refinancing access become the binding constraints. The observable trigger is a fall in data center and networking sales below the third-quarter level. Primary downside path: a data center slowdown that cuts Commercial segment profit while acquisition debt and capital spending stay fixed. spans.text: # CP-0 Source readiness: Ttm Technologies Inc (ttmi-1116942)
## Request

Source readiness for Ttm Technologies Inc (issuer ttmi-1116942), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is whether the five supplied filings can support the financial foundation, business and governance, and fundamental credit analyses, and which other analyses they cannot support.
## Sources

No upstream handoff was supplied: this module runs first.
## Findings
### Bottom line

The five filings support a filings-only financial, business and credit view of TTM Technologies, but only to 2026-09-28: the Epiq acquisition and the USD 1,100.0 million of term loans that funded it closed two days later and sit outside the reported statements.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 27; calculation C9

Reported debt of USD 1,659.0 million at that date excludes those loans, so any pro forma leverage must be built from stated transaction amounts and labelled as an estimate. No executed debt documents, ratings, market quotes, peer data or Epiq results were supplied, so covenant capacity, recovery, relative value and security selection cannot be worked from this set.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation C8
### Key findings

Four audited fiscal years (FY2022 to FY2025) and every 2026 quarter are covered, and the statements extracted cleanly: all five balance sheets foot, the three 2026 quarters add exactly to the nine-month sales and operating income, and year-end figures agree between the two annual reports. The latest filing was signed 21 days before the as-of date, so later events are not captured.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C7; calculation C10; calculation C11

The filings do not print a covenant ratio. The revolver carries two maintenance tests, a minimum interest cover of 2.50x and a maximum leverage of 4.50x, and management states compliance, so headroom cannot be established without the agreement's definitions. The executed credit agreements and indentures are listed as exhibits to earlier current reports but were not supplied.

Three selected analyses, Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit, are ready with limitations. Of the analyses outside this run, Earnings changes, Downside, Liquidity, Refinancing & LME, Rates, FX & hedging, Evidence validation, Committee decision and Short credit snapshot are also ready with limitations, while Peer benchmark, Earnings quality, Forward credit model, Ratings & triggers, Legal & covenants, Recovery & fulcrum, Security selection and Market-implied risk are conditional on documents the set does not carry.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Reported leverage is moderate but understates what creditors now hold: net debt of USD 767.5 million was 1.31x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 2026-09-28, before the USD 1,100.0 million Epiq purchase that, on stated amounts, lifts it to 3.20x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation C16; calculation C18; calculation C22; calculation C41

Earnings growth, not debt paydown, drove total leverage from 4.52x in FY2023 to 2.22x in FY2025. Free cash flow is thin: capital spending of USD 251.6 million left only USD 21.2 million of the USD 272.9 million operating cash flow of the first nine months of 2026, and that flow leaned on a USD 376.0 million rise in payables.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation C17; calculation C27; calculation C28; calculation C42
### Key findings

Carrying debt was essentially unchanged from FY2023 to FY2025, so the fall in total leverage from 4.52x to 2.22x came from earnings: EBITDA rose from USD 203.0 million to USD 411.9 million as net sales grew from USD 2,232.6 million to USD 2,906.3 million, and the goodwill impairments of FY2023 and FY2024, which reported EBITDA does not add back, ended. In 2026 the direction reversed: debt rose by USD 727.7 million to USD 1,643.9 million while cash rose by USD 375.1 million, so net debt rose by USD 352.6 million, mainly to pay USD 369.1 million, net of cash acquired, for Swiss Technology Group AG, and net leverage moved from 1.01x to 1.31x.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, pages 85–87; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C18; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C43

Cash interest cover rose from 4.24x in FY2023 to 8.92x in FY2025 and 12.72x on a last-twelve-months basis because EBITDA doubled while cash interest was broadly unchanged. That cover looks backward: scheduled interest of USD 65.0 million falls due within a year on debt at 2026-09-28, before the Incremental Facilities, and the 2034 senior unsecured notes alone cost USD 33.8 million a year, so 12.72x overstates the cover creditors now have.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 87; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 36; calculation C19; calculation C32; calculation C33; calculation C44

Operating cash flow was carried by working capital rather than earnings alone. In the first nine months of 2026 receivables and contract assets absorbed USD 574.9 million and payables supplied USD 376.0 million, and all working capital lines together were a net use of USD 169.7 million. Equipment of USD 167.3 million sat unpaid in payables, USD 104.7 million more than a year earlier, so cash capital spending of USD 251.6 million understates what has been committed, and income taxes payable of USD 50.6 million indicate tax expense still to be paid in cash. Free cash flow was USD 21.2 million against USD 5.8 million a year earlier.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation C28; calculation C29; calculation C38; calculation C37; calculation C27; calculation C45

Liquidity at 2026-09-28 was USD 1,610.2 million, cash of USD 876.3 million plus USD 733.9 million of revolver availability, with USD 241.1 million of the cash in foreign subsidiaries; it is stated before the Epiq payment and the USD 180.0 million revolver repayment that followed. The maturity ladder is light until 2029: USD 181.0 million falls in the rest of 2026, USD 5.0 million in 2027 and USD 3.0 million in 2028, then USD 504.0 million in 2029 and USD 386.0 million in 2030. The Incremental Facilities add USD 300.0 million maturing in 2031 and USD 800.0 million in 2033.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C25; calculation C21; calculation C24; calculation C46

At 2026-09-28 the first-priority secured term loan (USD 399.0 million) and revolver (USD 260.0 million) rank ahead of the 2029 and 2034 senior unsecured notes (USD 500.0 million each). Cumulative principal through the notes is 2.84x last-twelve-months EBITDA against 2.81x on carrying value. Operating and finance leases, supplier finance and customer deposits sit outside the debt lines.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; calculation C20; calculation C40; calculation C17; calculation C47

Contract liabilities were USD 202.3 million against USD 175.6 million at year-end 2025, long-term customer deposits fell from USD 23.5 million to USD 17.6 million after USD 5.8 million was refunded, and supplier finance obligations carried in payables rose from USD 12.5 million to USD 21.5 million. These are small beside payables of USD 1,032.7 million, but they fund working capital and would reverse if customers or banks withdrew.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C39; calculation C48

The issuer states no EBITDA, so EBITDA here is operating income plus depreciation and amortization, a stricter measure than a lender-defined one: stock-based compensation of USD 61.7 million and acquisition-related and other charges of USD 18.5 million in the first nine months of 2026 are charged against it. Capital spending is gross in the annual reports and net in the interim reports, so a last-twelve-months free cash flow is not calculable, and segment reporting changed twice, so annual segment history does not compare with 2026.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 87; calculation C35; calculation C49

After 2026-09-28 the Epiq purchase closed on 2026-09-30 for USD 1,100.0 million of cash, funded by the Incremental Facilities and part of the proceeds of the 2034 notes; USD 180.0 million of revolver debt was repaid; shares costing about USD 100.0 million were bought on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27, with a further USD 100.0 million authorized on 2026-10-27; and an agreement to buy Ophir Optics for USD 650.0 million, announced on 2026-10-19, is expected to close in the second quarter of 2027. The 2026 capital expenditure outlook is USD 410.0 million to USD 430.0 million.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C22; calculation C23; calculation C50
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence is that the Incremental Facilities of USD 1,100.0 million equal the Epiq price, so on stated amounts the cash and revolver availability of USD 1,610.2 million at 2026-09-28 was left largely in place, and the 3.20x pro forma net leverage overstates leverage if Epiq earns material EBITDA, which is not supplied. As an illustration only, USD 100.0 million of Epiq EBITDA would put pro forma net leverage at 2.73x. The view would change with Epiq's reported EBITDA and purchase accounting in the fourth quarter 2026 report, an adjusted EBITDA reconciliation, the revolver availability after closing, and the reported covenant ratios.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; calculation C25; calculation C22; calculation C34; calculation C51
### Limitations

Epiq's results, balance sheet and purchase price allocation are in no supplied document, so the pro forma figures use stated transaction amounts only and exclude Epiq's own earnings, cash and debt, fees and closing adjustments.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; Source readiness (CP-0)
The issuer's covenant ratios are not printed and the 2026 wording on term loan repayments is ambiguous, so scheduled amortization and covenant headroom are not established.

## Gaps

- Epiq's financial statements, results, balance sheet and purchase price allocation are not in any supplied document, so pro forma leverage cannot include Epiq's earnings, cash or debt; it restricts the post-closing leverage, cover and liquidity figures, severity High, and the action is the fourth quarter 2026 report or Epiq's own statements.

- The issuer states no EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA, so EBITDA is built from operating income plus depreciation and amortization for every period; it restricts comparison with lender-defined leverage and with covenant tests, severity Medium, and the action is an earnings release with a reconciliation.

- Covenant ratio values and definitions for the revolver tests are not printed, so covenant headroom is not calculable for any period; severity Medium, and the action is the executed credit agreement and compliance certificates.
- The undrawn committed facilities at the end of FY2023 are not in the supplied annual reports, so the FY2023 liquidity row has cash only; severity Low, and the action is the FY2023 annual report.

- Several income statement and cash flow cells are dashes in the source (impairment of goodwill, loss on extinguishment of debt, gain on sale of subsidiary, derivative losses, proceeds of capital-related government incentives and others) and are written as not supplied, not zero; severity Low, and the action is none beyond confirming the dashes mean nil.

- Some lines exist in only some reports (for example derivative losses appear only in the 2026 interim statements and purchases of equipment are gross in annual reports and net in interim reports), so those cells are not supplied for the other columns; severity Medium for capital spending, which makes last-twelve-months capital spending and free cash flow not calculable, and the action is a consistent capital spending series.

- The 2026 wording on term loan repayments is ambiguous between a quarterly and an annual 1% of the original principal; it restricts the scheduled amortization shown for the term loan; severity Medium, and the action is the credit agreement.

- Segment reporting changed in 2025 and again in 2026 and no annual series is on the 2026 basis, so segment trend across annual and interim periods is not comparable; severity Medium, and the action is a recast annual segment table.

- Acquisition accounting for Swiss Technology Group AG is provisional and the filing presents no pro forma information, so goodwill, intangibles and the post-acquisition earnings contribution may change; severity Low, and the action is the fourth quarter 2026 report.
- No quarterly statement for the fourth quarter of 2025 is supplied, so that quarter is derived as the full year less nine months and labelled calculated; severity Low, and the action is none.
- Period start dates are not printed and are set to the day after the previous period end; severity Low, and the action is none.

- The share of cash held by foreign subsidiaries, USD 241.1 million at 2026-09-28, may be subject to repatriation tax if remitted, although the issuer states no material unaccrued tax; severity Low, and the action is none.
- Capital spending is not split between maintenance and growth in any filing, so those lines are not supplied; severity Medium, and the action is management disclosure of the split.

- The pending Ophir Optics acquisition is not completed, so no net debt effect or pro forma figure is stated for it and its cells are not supplied; severity Low, and the action is the report after closing.
- The share repurchase is dated as a two-day window and not by purchase, so its date cell is not supplied; severity Low, and the action is none.
- No balance sheet at the end of the third quarter of 2025 is supplied, so the period-end working capital measures have no nine-month 2025 value; severity Low, and the action is none.

spans.text: # CP-1A Business & governance: Ttm Technologies Inc (ttmi-1116942)
## Request

Business, transaction, ownership and operating-model fact pack for Ttm Technologies Inc (issuer ttmi-1116942), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the five supplied filings and the Source readiness analysis; transactions after the 2026-09-28 balance sheet are described only as far as those filings describe them.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

TTM Technologies is now a larger, more acquisitive and more data-center-dependent credit than its last annual report shows, and creditors rely on an unseen USD 1,100.0 million acquisition, Epiq, closed two days after quarter end and funded entirely from new notes and term loans.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation F8

Trading is strong on the evidence supplied: nine-month net sales rose 43.2% and operating margin reached 11.3%. The documents give no Epiq results, no holder percentages and no leverage after the new borrowings, and three further acquisitions are pending, so the combined effect on creditors is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation F2; calculation F3; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 27
### Key findings

- Acquisitions now drive the risk profile more than operations do. Consideration announced or completed since 2026-06-17 totals USD 2,151.2 million: USD 401.2 million for STG (closed 2026-09-16), USD 1,100.0 million for Epiq (closed 2026-09-30) and USD 650.0 million for Ophir Optics (agreed 2026-10-19, closing expected in the second quarter of 2027). New debt of USD 1,600.0 million was raised between 2026-09-24 and 2026-09-30, which concentrates integration, leverage and refinancing risk in one quarter.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, pages 23–24; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation F7; calculation F8

- The earnings base has shifted toward AI-driven data center circuit boards, which makes cash flow more cyclical than the defense-heavy history suggests. Data center and networking was 39% of nine-month net sales against 30% a year earlier, while aerospace and defense fell to 37% from 45%; the Commercial segment was 62.3% of net sales against 53.3%. Management attributes the growth to continued build-out of AI data centers.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation F4; calculation F6

- Customer concentration is high and steady in sales but has risen in receivables. The five largest customers were 44% of nine-month net sales in both years, one customer was about 20% of third-quarter sales, and two customers held 30% of receivables at quarter end against one customer at 14% at the prior year-end.

- No sponsor, parent or controlling holder is identified, so the governance risk comes from management's capital allocation rather than sponsor extraction, but that rests on a proxy statement that was not supplied. Management has never paid a dividend, yet it repurchased about USD 100.0 million of shares on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27, about a month after raising USD 1,600.0 million of debt, and authorised a further USD 100.0 million program.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 78; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation F8

- Cash generation does not yet cover the investment program. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 272.9 million was almost fully absorbed by net capital spending of USD 251.6 million, and the STG purchase took a further USD 369.1 million net of cash acquired; operating cash flow leaned on a USD 376.0 million rise in supplier payables while receivables and contract assets absorbed USD 574.9 million.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation F9; calculation F10

- Reported figures stop before Epiq. The balance sheet date precedes the closing by two days, Epiq's initial accounting and financial information had not been received by the filing date, and the STG accounting is provisional, so every figure above describes TTM without its largest acquisition.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is earnings momentum and liquidity. Third-quarter segment operating margin was 18.5% in aerospace and defense and 21.1% in Commercial, against 16.3% and 14.7% a year earlier. Cash was USD 876.3 million, USD 733.9 million of revolver capacity was available, and management states compliance with every covenant at 2026-09-28. Epiq is described as adding critical technologies for defense customers, which, if its earnings are defense-linked and stable, would rebalance the mix toward aerospace and defense. Against that, the 75.3% fixed-rate share of debt predates the floating-rate term loans, and the cash balance appears to include the proceeds of the 2034 notes raised four days before quarter end, which were used after quarter end.

The view would improve if the fourth-quarter report shows Epiq earnings that comfortably service the USD 1,100.0 million price, if data center demand holds without a rise in customer concentration, and if the pending acquisitions are funded from cash flow rather than new debt. It would worsen if Epiq's earnings are thin or cyclical, if Ophir Optics is debt-funded on top of the September borrowings, or if share repurchases continue while capital spending runs ahead of operating cash flow.
### Limitations

- Epiq's financial statements and purchase price allocation were not received by the filing date, so the conclusion on whether the USD 1,100.0 million price is supported by earnings stays a statement about structure and funding, not about value.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling holder exists reflects what the documents disclose, not a confirmed fact; holder percentages, board independence and related-party dealings are not established.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 78

- The latest filing was signed 21 days before the as-of date, so the conclusion that three acquisitions are pending may be out of date and the status of ILFA, named in June but not in October, is not established.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-06-29_ttmi-20260629.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation F15
- Segment structure changed twice and end-market categories were recast, so the mix-shift conclusion compares recast figures and cannot be traced to a single annual series.

- Customer concentration is stated on different bases across filings (five largest, ten largest, one or two customers), so the conclusion that concentration is steady rests on the five-largest series only.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

TTM agreed on 2026-06-17 to buy two European companies, Swiss Technology Group AG (STG) and ILFA GmbH, in separate stock purchase agreements. The STG purchase closed on 2026-09-16 for cash of USD 401.2 million, with a deal-contingent cross-currency swap of USD 381.1 million against CHF 306.2 million to fix the Swiss franc cost, and the Q2 filing describes a planned revolver drawdown to finance it. STG makes rigid, rigid-flex and flex circuit boards and miniaturized microcircuits in Switzerland and Germany for surgical robotics, hearing aid, medical imaging and implantable-device customers and sits in the Commercial segment. Provisional amounts at quarter end were goodwill of USD 202.5 million, definite-lived intangibles of USD 111.0 million and property, plant and equipment of USD 44.4 million; no pro forma figures are shown because the filing calls the deal not material. The documents do not say whether the ILFA purchase closed.

On 2026-09-30, two days after the quarter ended, TTM bought all membership interests in EDS Intermediate Holding, LLC (Epiq) for cash of USD 1,100.0 million, subject to customary post-closing adjustments. The purchase agreement is dated 2026-08-15 and names EDS TopCo, LP, TTM Technologies North America, LLC and TTM Technologies, Inc. as parties besides Epiq, and a debt commitment letter of the same date from JPMorgan Chase Bank, Barclays Bank PLC and two Bank of America entities was filed alongside it. The filing says the deal is meant to provide critical technologies and innovative capabilities for aerospace and defense customers. It gives no Epiq revenue, earnings, assets, location or seller ownership and no purchase price allocation, because the information had not been received; preliminary accounting is promised in the fourth-quarter 2026 report.

Three financing steps shaped the debt. On 2026-06-01 the 2026 Credit Agreement replaced the term loan with a USD 400.0 million Amended Term Loan Facility (one-month Term SOFR plus 1.75%, due 2030-05-30) and replaced the USD 150.0 million U.S. and USD 150.0 million Asia asset-based facilities with a USD 1,000.0 million revolving facility due May 2031, of which USD 80.0 million was drawn to repay the Asia facility. On 2026-09-24 TTM issued USD 500.0 million of 6.750% senior unsecured notes due 2034-10-01 (7.05% effective rate), guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries and subject to special mandatory redemption had Epiq not closed. On 2026-09-30 the Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement added a USD 300.0 million Incremental Term Loan A due 2031-05-30 and a USD 800.0 million Incremental Term Loan B due 2033-09-30, guaranteed and secured on the same basis as the existing loans, and USD 180.0 million of revolver borrowings was repaid after quarter end. Only the revolver carries maintenance covenants: minimum interest coverage of 2.50:1.00 and maximum leverage of 4.50:1.00, rising to 5.00:1.00 for the quarter of a qualifying material acquisition and the next three quarters.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation F8

Further deals and shareholder returns follow. Ophir Optics, the Ophir Optics business of MKS Inc., is to be bought for USD 650.0 million in cash; the agreement was announced on 2026-10-19 and closing is expected in the second quarter of 2027, with funding not stated. Two further European acquisitions, called immaterial and not named, are expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026 subject to regulatory approvals. Management raised its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to USD 410.0 million to USD 430.0 million, citing a plan to invest a further USD 400.0 million in capacity for AI infrastructure. On 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27 TTM repurchased about 1,159 thousand shares for about USD 100.0 million, using up the 2025 program, and on 2026-10-27 the board authorised a new program of up to USD 100.0 million.

Not stated in the documents read: pricing of the incremental term loans, any leverage after the 2026-09-30 borrowings, Epiq's earnings and sellers, how Ophir Optics will be funded, and the funding source of the share repurchases.

spans.text: # CP-2 Fundamental credit: Ttm Technologies Inc (ttmi-1116942)
## Request

Fundamental credit synthesis for Ttm Technologies Inc (issuer ttmi-1116942), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the five supplied filings with the Source readiness, Financial foundation and Business & governance analyses; reported figures run to 2026-09-28 and later events are flagged, not blended in.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

TTM's fundamental credit is adequate and improving on earnings but now acquisition-dependent: net leverage of 1.31x at 2026-09-28 becomes 3.20x pro forma for the Epiq closing on 2026-09-30, and thin free cash flow leaves little cushion if AI-driven demand slows.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation G3; calculation G4

Earnings are the support: last-twelve-months EBITDA of USD 584.3 million is 2.88 times the USD 203.0 million of FY2023, and liquidity was USD 1,610.2 million before the Epiq payment. The 3.20x uses stated transaction amounts and excludes Epiq's own EBITDA, which is not supplied, so leverage after the acquisition is not established.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G1; calculation G5; calculation G4
### Key findings

- Earnings, not debt reduction, repaired the credit. Carrying debt was USD 917.8 million at FY2023 and USD 916.2 million at FY2025, yet total leverage fell from 4.52x to 2.22x as EBITDA doubled. It was 2.81x on a last-twelve-months basis at 2026-09-28, after the 2026 borrowings for the Swiss purchase and for Epiq.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G1; calculation G2

- The September 2026 acquisitions turn a low-leverage credit into a moderate-leverage one whose outcome depends on an unseen asset. Net leverage of 1.31x at 2026-09-28 is 3.20x pro forma for the Epiq closing on 2026-09-30, applied alone and excluding Epiq's EBITDA; Financial foundation illustrates that USD 100.0 million of Epiq EBITDA would give 2.73x. The Ophir Optics purchase of USD 650.0 million, if debt-funded, would add to it.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 24; calculation G3; calculation G4

- Free cash flow is the weak link and the investment program is accelerating. Nine-month operating cash flow of USD 272.9 million left only USD 21.2 million after USD 251.6 million of net capital spending, against USD 5.8 million a year earlier, and FY2025 free cash flow was negative USD 0.7 million. The 2026 capital spending outlook of USD 410.0 million to USD 430.0 million implies fourth-quarter spending of USD 158.4 million to USD 178.4 million if it is on the same basis as the nine-month figure, about twice the average quarterly pace.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G6; calculation G7

- Earnings now rest on one engine, the Commercial segment. It earned USD 360.5 million of segment operating income in nine months, more than the group's USD 343.8 million of operating income, and 64.8% of segment operating income against 52.8% a year earlier, while aerospace and defense income of USD 195.7 million was absorbed by USD 212.4 million of unallocated corporate costs and amortization. Management links the growth to AI data center build-out.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 31; calculation G8

- Liquidity and the maturity ladder are strengths, but interest cover looks backward. Liquidity of USD 1,610.2 million at 2026-09-28 is stated before the Epiq payment and the USD 180.0 million revolver repayment, and pro forma liquidity is not established. Nothing large matures until the 2029 notes: USD 504.0 million in 2029 and USD 386.0 million in 2030 are 53.6% of principal. Cash interest cover of 12.72x excludes the new loans, which are floating rate and add USD 11.0 million a year for each 100 bp rise in rates.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 43; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G5; calculation G9; calculation G10; calculation G11

- Customer concentration is high and has moved into receivables. The five largest customers were 44% of nine-month net sales, one customer was about 20% of third-quarter sales, and two customers held 30% of receivables at quarter end, so one payment delay would show quickly in operating cash flow, which already leans on a USD 376.0 million rise in supplier payables.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Financial policy is mixed rather than adverse. There is no sponsor and there has never been a dividend, but TTM repurchased about USD 100.0 million of shares on 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27 and authorised another USD 100.0 million, which is 6.25% of the USD 1,600.0 million of debt raised in September; Business & governance rates governance risk as medium.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 57; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation G13
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against caution is that the earnings base is large and still rising: EBITDA margin reached 15.3% on a last-twelve-months basis, reported net leverage was only 1.31x before Epiq, management states covenant compliance, and long-term defense contracts carried USD 463.5 million of remaining obligations at 2026-09-28. If Epiq earns material EBITDA, the 3.20x overstates leverage, and the Incremental Facilities equal the Epiq price, so the revolver headroom was largely preserved. Epiq is described as adding technology for defense customers, which could rebalance a mix that is now led by data center sales.

The view would improve if the fourth-quarter report shows Epiq EBITDA near or above the illustration, free cash flow turns clearly positive after capital spending, and Ophir Optics is funded without new debt. It would weaken if data center and networking sales fall from their third-quarter level of USD 498.0 million, if capital spending runs at the implied fourth-quarter pace without a matching rise in operating cash flow, or if repurchases continue while leverage is elevated after the acquisitions.

### Limitations

- Epiq's EBITDA, cash, debt and fees are not supplied, so the pro forma net leverage of 3.20x is a stated-amounts figure and the conclusion on post-acquisition leverage is a range around it, not a point.

### Strengths and weaknesses

The main strengths are these. First, earnings have more than doubled since FY2023 and drove total leverage from 4.52x to 2.22x at FY2025, which gives the debt a much larger earnings base and lowers refinancing risk. Second, liquidity of USD 1,610.2 million at 2026-09-28 and a maturity ladder with only USD 181.0 million due before 2029 give time to digest the acquisitions. Third, the defense franchise is anchored in long-term contracts with USD 463.5 million of remaining performance obligations and a US Navy radar position, which supports a steadier base beside the data center cycle. Fourth, margin gains in both segments show operating leverage working in the issuer's favour while volumes are high. Fifth, there is no sponsor and no dividend, so no external owner draws cash out.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation G1; calculation G2; calculation G5; calculation G11

The main weaknesses are these. First, the Epiq purchase and the pending Ophir Optics purchase raise net leverage to 3.20x pro forma while the target's earnings are unseen, which makes the next two quarters decisive for creditors. Second, free cash flow is thin and capital spending is stepping up, so deleveraging depends on EBITDA growth rather than cash generation. Third, earnings are concentrated in the Commercial segment and in AI data center demand, which makes cash flow more cyclical than the defense history suggests. Fourth, customer concentration and the reliance on supplier payables expose operating cash flow to a single payment or terms change. Fifth, the new term loans are floating rate and the reported interest cover of 12.72x does not include them.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation G4; calculation G6; calculation G8; calculation G9; calculation G10

### Company description

TTM Technologies makes printed circuit boards, RF and microwave components and assemblies, and engineered mission systems, and sells to equipment makers, contract manufacturers, distributors and governments. About 59% of nine-month net sales came from operations outside the United States, revenue is mostly recognized over time as customer-specific products are built, and the business is not seasonal. The credit link is that long-term defense contracts and a diversified customer list support cash-flow visibility, while the AI-driven commercial boom, high fixed costs and acquisition debt make debt service more cyclical than the defense history alone would suggest.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 39; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Ownership and group structure

TTM is a widely held public company with no sponsor, parent or controlling holder named in the documents read, so sponsor extraction is not the risk; holder percentages sit in a proxy statement not supplied. The borrower is the parent, the notes and credit facilities are guaranteed by domestic subsidiaries only, and 63.1% of long-lived assets and USD 241.1 million of cash sit outside the United States, so the guarantee package covers domestic subsidiaries only and claims on foreign operating assets rank behind those subsidiaries' own creditors, which is structural subordination; foreign subsidiary borrowers may draw up to USD 300.0 million of the revolver. Epiq joined as a guarantor on 2026-09-30. Ranking and collateral are for the Structural priority analysis; this module records that the secured term loan and revolver pledge only 65% of certain foreign subsidiaries' stock.
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue rests on two engines: defense electronics sold through government budgets and long-term contracts, and commercial circuit boards for AI data centers, automotive and medical customers. Data center and networking was 39% of nine-month net sales against 30%, aerospace and defense 37% against 45%, and long-term defense contracts carried USD 463.5 million of remaining obligations with about 55% to be recognized within 12 months. Pricing power is only partly evidenced: gross margin rose 2.0 percentage points to 22.4% on volume and mix, quick-turn work earns premium pricing, but no contract pass-through of raw material costs is described. Revenue is therefore predictable in defense, cyclical and concentrated in data center and networking, and moderately recurring overall; the implication is that cash flow durability is adequate rather than strong.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation G12
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Management states that operating costs are relatively fixed and that small revenue shortfalls reduce operating margin, so operating leverage works both ways: gross margin rose to 22.4% and operating margin to 11.3% on higher volume, and the same fixed base would amplify a slowdown. Unallocated corporate costs are also growing, with stock-based compensation of USD 61.7 million against USD 29.6 million and other corporate costs of USD 103.5 million against USD 66.4 million in nine months, which reduces the margin that segment profit converts into group profit. Raw materials such as copper and gold are exposed to price swings and some components have sole sources. Margins can be defended against moderate volume pressure, but not against a sharp fall in data center orders.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 28; calculation G8
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital spending is heavy and rising: gross purchases of USD 292.6 million in FY2025 were 10.1% of net sales, nine-month net purchases of USD 251.6 million in 2026 were 8.2%, and equipment of USD 167.3 million was unpaid in payables. The filings do not split maintenance from growth spending, so flexibility cannot be measured, although the new Eau Claire, Penang and Syracuse capacity is clearly growth-driven and could be slowed. Operating cash flow converts 58.5% of nine-month EBITDA, and free cash flow after capital spending was USD 21.2 million, so EBITDA does not yet translate into durable free cash flow for deleveraging.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 6; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G6; calculation G16
### Competitive forces

Rivalry is intense: printed circuit boards are fragmented with larger, lower-cost Chinese and Taiwanese competitors, while defense systems compete with BAE Systems, Curtiss-Wright, Leonardo DRS, Mercury Systems and Sanmina; the implication is price pressure in commercial boards and a premium for qualified defense work. New entrants face facility security clearances and customer qualification in defense, while the annual report notes that new competitors may enter commercial boards, which limits pricing power there. Buyer power is high because a few customers and contract manufacturers account for a large share of sales and receivables. Supplier power is moderate: laminates and chemicals are broadly available, but some components for assemblies have limited or sole sources. Substitution risk is not discussed in the documents read.
### Macro and policy factors

Policy and currency factors are material to this credit. Both the US and Chinese governments have put circuit boards under tariffs, about 59% of nine-month sales come from non-US operations, and costs and cash are exposed to the Chinese yuan, Malaysian ringgit and Swiss franc, with a net investment hedge on the Swiss purchase. Defense sales depend on US budget appropriations and contract terminations, and export rules shape competition. The credit effect is margin and cash volatility that is partly outside management's control.
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths are the earnings recovery, liquidity, the defense contract base and operating leverage; weaknesses are thin free cash flow, customer concentration, floating-rate acquisition debt and an unseen Epiq. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are Epiq and Ophir Optics earnings that add defense technology and diversify away from data center demand, and capacity additions that convert growth into cash. Threats that could weaken credit quality are an AI capital spending slowdown, tariffs on circuit boards, a payment delay by a top customer and further debt-funded acquisitions.

### Financial profile and credit quality

The financial profile supports a view of adequate credit quality. Supports are the rise in EBITDA, liquidity before the Epiq payment, a light maturity ladder and an audited, controlled reporting base; constraints are leverage that jumps to 3.20x pro forma, free cash flow of only USD 21.2 million, concentration in one segment and floating-rate debt. The trend is improving to 2026-09-28 and reversing at the Epiq closing. Missing datapoints are Epiq's EBITDA, cash and debt, covenant definitions and headroom, post-closing liquidity, peer and rating data, and the split of capital spending.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-29_ttmi-20251229.htm.jsonl, page 82; calculation G3; calculation G4; calculation G5; calculation G6
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are AI data center capacity demand, defense budgets and program bookings, and new capacity at Eau Claire, Penang and Syracuse, which together support growth and margin. The headwinds are integration of STG, Epiq and Ophir Optics, capital spending that exceeds operating cash flow, higher interest on floating-rate loans, tariffs and currency swings. Over three to five years the main questions are whether AI demand proves durable rather than cyclical, whether Epiq earnings cover its price, and whether the 2029 notes and 2030 term loan balance are refinanced at acceptable cost; refinancing confidence rests on earnings, which is why a data center slowdown is the key risk to it.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 32; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-06-29_ttmi-20260629.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 15; calculation G11
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a pause in AI data center orders or the loss of volume at one of the largest customers; one customer was about 20% of third-quarter sales and the five largest were 44% of nine-month sales. The first operational break is lower volume in the Commercial segment, whose fixed cost base would cut margin quickly, and that segment supplied more profit than the whole group. Financially, EBITDA falls while the pro forma net debt of USD 1,867.5 million stays, so net leverage rises above 3.20x, free cash flow turns negative because committed capital spending continues, and the cash cushion funds the gap. Management levers are slowing growth capital spending, suspending repurchases and not closing Ophir Optics; whether they suffice depends on the maintenance share of spending, which is not stated, and on covenant definitions, which are not supplied. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress in a moderate downturn because liquidity was large and no large maturity falls before 2029, but leverage-based tests and refinancing access become the binding constraints. The observable trigger is a fall in data center and networking sales below the third-quarter level. Primary downside path: a data center slowdown that cuts Commercial segment profit while acquisition debt and capital spending stay fixed.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-28_ttmi-20260928.htm.jsonl, page 17; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation G4; calculation G8
### Overall credit view

Overall, TTM presents an adequate business profile supported by a recovered earnings base, ample pre-acquisition liquidity and a defense contract anchor, but credit quality is constrained by acquisition-driven leverage, thin free cash flow and concentration in one segment and a few customers. Cash-flow durability appears adequate rather than strong because operating cash flow depends on supplier payables and capital spending is rising. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on Epiq's earnings, data center demand and market access for the 2029 notes and 2030 term loan. The primary downside path is a data center slowdown against fixed acquisition debt and capital commitments. Further analysis would require Epiq's financials, covenant definitions and compliance certificates, post-closing liquidity and rating or peer data. Fundamental credit review completed with limitations. Top risk: acquisition leverage built on an unseen target while free cash flow is thin.
